comparisons.peer_summary: First-Line Units (FLUs) and control functions are responsible for managing all aspects of their businesses, including compliance and operational risk. They must understand their processes and risks, monitor controls, conduct quality assurance, adhere to risk appetite limits, and proactively identify and escalate risks to strengthen organizational resiliency.
comparisons.comparison: Both GS and BAC define their first line of defense as consisting of revenue-producing units that bear primary responsibility for managing risk and designing/executing controls. GS explicitly lists corporate functions like Conflicts Resolution, Controllers, and Engineering as part of this line, while BAC uses the term 'First-Line Units (FLUs)' to encompass business units and control functions responsible for managing all aspects of their businesses, including compliance and operational risk. Both disclosures emphasize that the first line must understand their processes, monitor controls, and actively identify and manage risks.

sentences.text: Our first line of defense consists of our revenue-producing units, Conflicts Resolution, Controllers, Engineering, Corporate Treasury and certain other corporate functions.
The first line of defense is responsible for its risk-generating activities, as well as for the design and execution of controls to mitigate such risks.
FLUs and control functions are first and foremost responsible for managing all aspects of their businesses, including their compliance and operational risk.

FLUs and control functions are required to understand their business processes and related risks and controls, including third-party dependencies and the related regulatory requirements, and monitor and report on the effectiveness of the control environment.

comparisons.peer_topic: Head of Technology and Business Enablement Role and Background
comparisons.peer_summary: Citi's Head of Technology and Business Enablement, who reports directly to the CEO, holds overall responsibility for first-line defense cyber and information security programs and has over 30 years of experience in the financial services industry.
comparisons.comparison: Both GS and Citi identify 'first line of defense' components that include specific corporate functions beyond just revenue-generating trading units. GS lists Corporate Treasury, Engineering, and Controllers as part of the first line, whereas Citi assigns overall responsibility for first-line cyber and information security programs to the Head of Technology and Business Enablement. Both disclosures highlight the integration of specialized corporate functions (technology/controls) into the first-line risk management structure.

comparisons.peer_topic: Three lines of defense model and responsibilities
comparisons.peer_summary: The Firm employs a "three lines of defense" model for risk management. The first line (LOBs, Treasury, CIO) owns risks and executes controls; the second line (IRM) independently measures and challenges risk activities and sets policies; the third line (Internal Audit) provides independent assessment of governance and controls.
comparisons.comparison: JPM and GS both describe the first line of defense as comprising Line of Business (LOB)/revenue-producing units and specific corporate functions (Treasury, CIO/Technology, Engineering, Controllers), with the explicit responsibility of owning risks and executing controls. JPM provides a more granular definition by separating the lines of defense (IRM as second, Internal Audit as third) and explicitly stating that the first line owns the risk identification and control design, mirroring GS's statement that the first line is responsible for 'design and execution of controls to mitigate such risks.'
